'''Serge Fedorovich Timashev''' (Russian: Сергей Федорович Тимашев, born September 29, 1937, in [[Irbit]], [[Sverdlovsk Oblast]], [[Soviet Union]]) is a Russian [[scientist]] performing research for USPolyResearch. He is best known for his work in [[Flicker noise|flicker-noise]] [[spectroscopy]] (extraction of information from chaotic signals),<ref name="fns1">{{cite book |title=Flicker-Noise Spectroscopy: Information in Chaotic Signals (In Russian) |last=Timashev |first=Serge F |year=2008 |publisher=Fizmatlit |location=Moscow |isbn=978-5-9221-0878-2}}</ref><ref name="fns2">{{cite journal|author1=Timashev SF |author2=Polyakov YuS |title=Review of Flicker Noise Spectroscopy in Electrochemistry |journal=Fluctuation and Noise Letters|volume=7|issue=2|pages=R15–R47|year=2007|doi=10.1142/S0219477507003829|arxiv=0812.0030}}</ref><ref name="fns3">{{cite journal|author1=Yulmetyev RM |author2=Demin SA |author3=Panischev OYu |author4=Hänggi P |author5=Timashev SF |author6=Vstovsky GV |title=Regular and Stochastic Behavior of Parkinsonian Pathological Tremor Signals |journal=Physica A|volume=369|pages=655–678|year=2006|doi=10.1016/j.physa.2006.01.077|arxiv = physics/0603030 |bibcode = 2006PhyA..369..655Y|issue=2 }}</ref><ref name="fns4">{{cite journal|author1=Descherevsky AV |author2=Lukk AA |author3=Sidorin AYa |author4=Vstovsky GV |author5=Timashev SF |title=Flicker-Noise Spectroscopy in Earthquake Prediction Research |journal=Natural Hazards and Earth System Sciences|volume=3|issue=3/4|pages=159–164|year=2003|doi=10.1016/j.pce.2003.09.017|bibcode = 2004PCE....29..389T }}</ref> [[physical chemistry]] ([[membrane processes]]),<ref  name="membrane1">{{cite book |title=Physical Chemistry of Membrane Processes|last=Timashev |first=Serge F |year=1991 |publisher=Ellis Horwood |location=Chichester | isbn=978-0-13-662982-5}}</ref><ref name="membrane2">{{cite journal |vauthors=Timashev SF, Valuev VV, etal |title=Pervaporation Induced by Electric Current |journal=J. Membr. Sci.|volume=91|pages=249–258|year=1994|doi=10.1016/0376-7388(94)80086-3|issue=3}}</ref> kinetics  of chemical processes (diffusion in energy space),<ref  name="kinet1">{{cite book |title=Methods of Physicochemical Kinetics (In Russian) |last=Tunitsky |first=NN |author2=Kaminsky VA |author3=Timashev SF |year=1972|publisher=Khimiya|location=Moscow}}</ref><ref  name="kinet2">{{cite book |title=Kinetics of Diffusion Controlled Chemical Process (In Russian) |last=Ovchinnikov|first=AA |author2=Timashev SF |author3=Belyi AA |year=1989|publisher=Nova Science Publishers|location=New York|isbn=978-0-941743-52-5}}</ref> [[quantum physics]] ([[semiconductors]]),<ref>{{cite journal|author=Timashev SF|title=Thermal Ionization of "Deep" Centers in Semiconductors in High-Intensity Electric Fields |journal=Sov. Solid State Physics |volume=14|pages=2621–2625|year=1972}}</ref> and Earth/space science (mechanism of global changes and [[evolution]]).<ref name="bio1">{{cite journal|author=Timashev SF|title=Physical Chemistry of Global Changes in the Biosphere |journal=Russ. J. Phys. Chem. |volume=67|issue=1|pages=145–149|year=1993}}</ref><ref name="bio2">{{cite journal|author1=Kostuchenko IG |author2=Timashev SF |title=Flicker-Noise in Processes of Solar Activity |journal=Int. J. Bifurc. Chaos |volume=8|issue=4|pages=805–811|year=1998|doi=10.1142/S0218127498000607|bibcode = 1998IJBC....8..805K }}</ref>

==Biography==
Timashev holds [[Master of Science|MS]] in [[Physics]] from the [[Moscow State University]] (1960), [[PhD]] in [[nuclear physics]] from the [[Institute of Theoretical and Experimental Physics]] ([[Moscow]], 1966), and [[Doktor nauk|DSc]] in physics and [[mathematics]] from the [[Institute of Semiconductor Physics]] ([[Novosibirsk]], 1975). His major job track record includes senior researcher (1969 to 1979) at the Institute of Physical Chemistry, [[USSR Academy of Science]], Moscow; head of [[membrane process]] [[laboratory]] (1979 to present) at the [[Karpov Institute of Physical Chemistry]], Moscow; professor in [[molecular physics]] (1990 to 1994) at the [[Moscow Engineering Physics Institute]]; [[professor]] in physics (1997 to present) at the [[Peoples' Friendship University of Russia]]; senior researcher (2005 to present) at USPolyResearch.

==Scientific achievements==
Timashev developed a flicker-noise spectroscopy method<ref name=FNS>{{cite web|title=Flicker-Noise Spectroscopy Toolkit|url=https://gitlab.com/ypolyakov/fns|author=Yuriy Polyakov|author2=Serge Timashev|accessdate=27 December 2020}}</ref> for extracting information from the chaotic signals produced by complex systems, which can be used for analyzing and predicting the behavior of these systems ([[earthquake prediction]], [[EKG]] evaluation, Parkinsonian tremor signal evaluation, random electrochemical processes, etc.)<ref name="fns1" /><ref name="fns2" /><ref name="fns3" /><ref name="fns4" /> He discovered the phenomenon of switching conductivity for surface-modified [[ion exchange]] [[polymeric membranes]] and electropervaporation effect.<ref name="membrane1" /><ref name="membrane2" /> He also described the role of chemical and solar factors in the [[biosphere]] evolution.<ref name="bio1" /><ref name="bio2" /> The total number of papers and books published by him is more than 300. He currently serves on the Editorial Advisory Boards of Russ. J. Phys. Chem., Russ. J. Electrochem., Colloid J., and J. Water Chem. Technol.{{citation needed|date=September 2015}}

==Honors and awards==
Timashev received [[Russian Federation]] Government's Prize in Science and Technology (1995), Ernest Oppenheimer Memorial Trust (WD Wilson Visiting Fellowship, South Africa, 1996), and Russian Federation's Distinguished Scientist (1998).{{citation needed|date=September 2015}}
